Subject: Performance SLO qualification - Nova Retail (follow-up)

Hi Tom / Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier - good to meet the Nova Retail team. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we all have the same assumptions for the SLO qualification:

Recap (as discussed)
- Primary product: customer support chat and in-app assistant for checkout flows.
- Traffic profile: peak concurrency ~100 active sessions, steady-state 150-200 reqs/s, bursting to ~400 reqs/s for flash events.
- Response sizes: median ~120 tokens, ~30% of requests up to ~512 tokens.
- Required behaviour: streaming partial tokens to the UI (low-latency first-byte / incremental).

Target SLOs you mentioned
- p95 time-to-first-token <= 200 ms for typical 120-token responses (streaming).
- p95 end-to-end generation <= 350 ms for 256-token responses (non-streaming tail allowance).
- Sustained throughput: 150-200 reqs/s with ability to absorb bursts to 400 reqs/s.

Cost / performance levers we'll evaluate with you
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token compute by overlapping attention work - we can tune batch window and max batch size to balance p95 latency vs cost.
- Prefix/KV caching: cache repeated context (product metadata, user profile) to reduce repeated compute on warm sessions.
- Quantization profiles: 8-bit and 4-bit profiles (we recommend starting with a calibrated 4-bit quantized run to measure quality delta).
- Model variants: run a smaller quantized 13B variant for asynchronous or lower-cost flows and a larger 34-70B variant behind the critical path with aggressive batching/fallback.
- Streaming config: chunk size and tokenization thresholds - small chunks reduce first-byte latency but increase per-token overhead.

Concrete next steps
1) Please share a small sample of request/response sizes (CSV or JSON) and a representative traffic hour (timestamps + payload sizes) - that will let us estimate batching efficiency and cache hit rates.
2) We'll run a 2-hour perf qualification in our test cluster using your sample traffic and two quantization profiles (q8/q4) and two model variants; deliverable: p95/p99 latency breakdown and token cost estimates.
3) Technical deep-dive with Rishi (infrastructure) next week to define batch settings and streaming contract (20-30 minutes).

I've attached a short SLO template and our cost levers doc for your review.

If those next steps look right, I'll schedule the perf run for next week and loop in our infra team.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications on our side:
- Tighten the p95 desired target to 200 ms time-to-first-token if possible - the UX team flagged anything above that as a noticeable delay in chat.
- For tails: p95 end-to-end for 512-token responses should be <= 500 ms if we can't hit 350 ms across the board (we know long responses are harder).
- Streaming is a hard requirement for the chat UI - partial tokens must flow as soon as available.

I'll get you a 60-minute sample of traffic (UTC logs) and a CSV with payload sizes by EOD tomorrow.

Hi Tom / Marissa -

Thanks for the details - quick technical notes from the infra side before the perf run:

Batching / runtime config suggestions (initial)- Continuous batching: target effective batch size 48-64 tokens for throughput-heavy windows. For latency-sensitive paths (time-to-first-token target ~200 ms), set a short micro-batching window (max coalesce latency ~6-10 ms) and a max batch size cap so we don't inflate p95.
- Max concurrency: provision for 120 concurrent sessions in the test to reproduce bursts; we'll scale GPUs up/down to match your reported 400 req/s bursts.
- Streaming: use chunked streaming with 16-32 token chunks for the UI. We recommend a tokenization-aware chunker to avoid splitting multibyte tokens.

Caching and quantization- Prefix/KV caching: if ~40% of sessions share product metadata, expect ~15-25% token cost reduction from caching on warm traffic. We'll estimate this once we see your sample.
- Quantization: run side-by-side q8 (fast, minimal quality delta) and q4 (lower cost, needs calibration). For many workloads q4 is viable; we do a quick eval on 200 samples to measure generation quality drop.

Model variants and fallback
- Plan: primary = 34B q8 quant profile for critical flows; fallback = 13B q4 for non-critical/low-cost flows. Automated routing policy can route by latency tier or customer segment to keep UX stable.

Perf run ask (to prepare)
- Traffic sample (CSV or ndjson) with timestamps, token counts, and whether request is streaming or non-streaming.
- A few representative prompts (20-50) for quality/regression checks.

I'll coordinate with infra to provision a 4-GPU test cluster (A100 equivalent) and run the 2-hour qualification once we have the sample. We'll return a short results pack (latency percentiles, token-costs, and suggested config).

Happy to join the Tue/Wed morning slot - toss me a few times and I'll confirm.

- Rishi
